Postgraduate research
Our standard (full time) PhD programme is four years in duration and is eligible for University scholarships. Visit the Graduate School website for further information on Mathematics and Statistics postgraduate degrees and on available scholarships.
PhD research topics
You can find example projects that are currently available at the Mathematics thesis topics and Statistics thesis topics. You can also visit the School of Mathematics and Statistics Research pages to see what other research there is and what opportunities there might be for projects
Applications
We consider applications from UK, EU and other international students for our full-time and part-time PhD and research masters programmes.
Shortlisting and review of applications for scholarships will begin on 1 January and will continue until all funded places have been awarded. Applications are still accepted after 1 January and will be considered for any remaining scholarship opportunities.

Martingale Foundation Scholarships
Students from low socioeconomic backgrounds who are interested in postgraduate research in mathematics may be eligible for a fully funded Martingale Scholarship, which provides financial support, professional development, and application guidance. Find out more and at the Martingale Foundation Scholarships page.
James McCune Smith Scholarships
The James McCune Smith PhD Scholarships support Black UK domiciled students undertaking doctoral research at the University of Glasgow through fully funded study, professional development opportunities, mentoring, and industry placements. Find out more about the scheme and future application rounds at the James McCune Smith Scholarships.
Maclaurin Scholarships
Maclaurin Scholarships provides an opportunity for talented students to undertake PhD study in the mathematical sciences while also gaining teaching experience by contributing to the School of Mathematics and Statistics extensive teaching programme. This is a five-year funded PhD scholarship which includes teaching duties. If you would like to be considered for a Maclaurin Scholarship please indicate this on your application form.
PhD with integrated study
The PhD with integrated study programme is a four-year PhD programme beginning with a nine month taught component which gives you comprehensive training before you embark on the research component of your PhD. This programme is particularly well suited to students who do not have the required background knowledge in the subject to begin a PhD immediately.
This programme is not eligible for our university scholarships.
Partnership PhD
The Partnership PhD programme provides an opportunity for industry employees to undertake a PhD project co-developed with the University of Glasgow and aligned with the research needs of the company.
Students under this programme will spend the majority of the PhD with their employer receiving support from an industrial and academic supervisor.
How to apply
Visit the Graduate School website for full instructions on how to apply online to study on our PhD and research masters programmes as well as information on English language requirements for the programmes. You can also find more information about applying on the University's How to apply for a postgraduate research degree page.
